definition: The knowledge graph is a deterministic, cache-backed graph of the magus domain: projects, targets, spells, ops, charms, modules, methods, and diagnostics, connected by verified relations (depends_on, contains, uses, references, documents). Every node and edge is extracted or rubric-inferred from workspace sources - no LLM pass - so it is safe to rebuild implicitly and query instead of grepping.

coverage
nodes.doc: coverage is the only public entry: a label, a percentage figure ("56.8", trailing "%" optional), and a corner radius (3 = rounded, 0 = square). The color is derived from the figure, never passed. Throws on a non-numeric figure.

nodes.label: flat_badge
nodes.doc: flat_badge builds the SVG: a grey label cell, a colored value cell, centered text. Private - the color arrives already derived.

nodes.label: halve
nodes.doc: halve turns a doubled coordinate back into "42" or "40.5". Positions are kept as 2x ints so a half-pixel midpoint survives integer division.

nodes.label: normalize_percent
nodes.doc: normalize_percent drops a trailing "%", so "56.8" and "56.8%" both work. The figure stays a string and is shown verbatim; a float round-trip would drift "100.0" to "100".

nodes.label: severity_color
nodes.doc: severity_color maps coverage to color: red below 50, up through orange, yellow, yellowgreen, green, to brightgreen at 90.

nodes.label: whole_percent
nodes.doc: whole_percent reads a figure's integer part ("56.8" -> 56). std\parseInt returns null on non-numeric input, which we turn into a clear error so a bad figure fails loudly instead of rendering wrong.

nodes.label: ci
nodes.doc: 'ci' is the conventional anchor that `magus affected ci` keys off. magus does not hardcode its steps - compose them here with ctx.needs. magus runs ci read-only. Each stage declares its own prerequisites so the DAG is expressed as edges: ci fans out lint/build/test in parallel; they each wait for format, which waits for generate, which waits for preflight. Shared deps run once.

nodes.label: ci
nodes.doc: 'ci' is the anchor `magus affected ci` keys off: the lint gate (tsc), the unit tests, the build-plus-drift-gate, and the advisory audit, all first-class ci steps.

nodes.label: diffdemo_generate
nodes.doc: build bundles the whole app into gen/ (esbuild via pnpm: the surface bundles + CSS, then copy-static assembles index/manifest/sw + scaffolds + assets) and gates on drift: a clean checkout only goes dirty when a source edit was not rebuilt and committed. The `rw` charm (`build:rw`) keeps the result instead of gating. esbuild is pinned (mise), so the output is byte-stable and the gate holds. Regenerates the Diff showcase's changeset from its .patch fixture.  The showcase renders with NO daemon, so it cannot a

nodes.label: format
nodes.doc: `format:rw` maintains declared source inputs.

nodes.label: install
nodes.doc: pnpm, NOT npm: .npmrc's minimum-release-age supply-chain gate is the reason. Always let pnpm validate the install. An interrupted install leaves a node_modules that EXISTS but is incomplete, and the isDir guard this replaced read that as ready, handing the missing packages straight to tsc/esbuild. Reached once per invocation through preflight, which every target below already needs, so the unconditional --frozen-lockfile costs about a second on a warm tree and never races itself.

nodes.label: lint
nodes.doc: lint keeps TypeScript, CSS, and source formatting errors out of the console CI gate.

nodes.label: security
nodes.doc: security audits the dependency tree against the npm advisory database.  --prod, not the whole tree, and that is the whole design. An unscoped audit reports the dev toolchain too - today a stylelint -> table -> ajv -> fast-uri advisory - which never reaches a browser and cannot be fixed from here. A gate that fails on something you cannot act on is a gate that gets muted, which is how six stale skip_cache workarounds happened. This fails only on what actually ships.  It is NOT folded into lint: lint is cache

nodes.label: test
nodes.doc: test runs the node:test suite over the bundled *.test.ts (the shell/view/tiling/keymap unit tests) and renders a line-coverage badge from the run.  The suite runs Node THREE times on purpose and that split is load-bearing: happy-dom installs localStorage/sessionStorage as getter-only, and several tests stub them by assignment, so applying the DOM setup globally (one --import for everything) breaks them. Unifying the runs was tried and reverted.  Which is why the figure needs lcov.mergePercent rather than lc

nodes.label: isGeneratedSource
nodes.doc: isGeneratedSource reports whether a Go source body carries the marker.  The scan stops at the package clause: the convention places the marker in the header, and stopping there keeps a passing mention of the phrase in ordinary code (a comment ABOUT generated files, of which this repo has several) from silently excluding a hand-written file from coverage.

nodes.label: modulePath
nodes.doc: modulePath reads the module path from a go.mod body. A coverage profile names files by import path, so this is what maps them back onto disk - derived rather than hardcoded so a module rename cannot silently disable the filter.

nodes.label: stripGenerated
nodes.doc: stripGenerated removes every coverage block belonging to a generated file.  It rewrites the PROFILE rather than filtering `go tool cover -func` output, because the percentage is a ratio of statements: dropping lines from the rendered report and re-averaging the per-function percentages would weight a one-statement function the same as a hundred-statement one. Keeping the profile as the unit means `go tool cover` still computes the total, and it stays exact.  prefix is the module path plus a trailing slash;

nodes.label: findReleasePost
nodes.doc: findReleasePost sets site.releaseBlogURL to the post whose frontmatter `release:` names the newest release's version, or leaves it "" when no post claims it.  The claim lives on the POST, not on the release manifest: a release need not have a post at all, and releases/*.yaml mirrors the Go ReleaseManifest that freezes index.json's v1 schema, so an optional docs-only field has no business there. It also means a post can be written and merged ahead of the tag it names, and starts announcing itself the moment

nodes.label: isPublishablePost
nodes.doc: isPublishablePost reports whether blog/<name> should be rendered at all: a .md file that is not the index, not an _underscored fixture, not marked `draft: true` in its frontmatter, and not dated past the build (isFuturePost).  A draft stays committed in the repo and renders NOWHERE - no post page, no blog index entry, no feed item, no announcement-bar link - so unfinished writing can be reviewed in a pull request without shipping to the site. The underscore prefix already skipped a file, but that is the fix

nodes.label: renderBlogIndex
nodes.doc: renderBlogIndex writes gen/blog/index.html, a reverse-chronological list of the collected posts. Runs AFTER renderBlogPost has populated site.blogPosts. A plain <ul> under renderPage(), so it inherits nav/breadcrumb/footer.

nodes.label: renderBlogPager
nodes.doc: renderBlogPager renders the prev/next links between posts, ordered by date newest-first so "prev" is newer and "next" is older (timeline intuition). Falls back to filename order when a post lacks a date.

nodes.label: renderBlogPost
nodes.doc: renderBlogPost renders one blog/<file>.md as its own directory-index page. base is the basename (e.g. "2026-07-01-hello-blog.md"); the URL is date-scoped blog/YYYY/MM/DD/slug/ (via blogURLPath), so permalinks sort by date and never collide across years. Post metadata is captured into site.blogPosts for the index page.

nodes.label: llmsIndexBody
nodes.doc: llmsIndexBody builds gen/llms.txt (the llms.txt convention): an H1, a one-line summary, then every docs page as "- [title](base+url): description", sorted by URL for a byte-stable artifact. base is the link prefix (baseURL, else "/"). Links point at each page's <url>index.md Markdown sibling, so an agent fetches clean content. Pure so a unit test can pin the output.

nodes.label: writeLLMsIndex
nodes.doc: writeLLMsIndex writes gen/llms.txt from the collected docs corpus. Links are absolute under baseURL when set (so an external agent can follow them), else root-relative.

nodes.label: writeSEOFiles
nodes.doc: writeSEOFiles writes sitemap.xml + robots.txt from the real page URLs (sorted, so byte-stable), each an absolute baseURL loc - "index.html" maps to the bare site root. Aliases are omitted (only canonical pages belong in a sitemap). Gated on baseURL so the site can ship dark until the host is confirmed. robots points crawlers at the sitemap.

nodes.label: renderBlogAtom
nodes.doc: renderBlogAtom writes gen/public/atom/blog.atom.xml: an Atom 1.0 feed of site.blogPosts, newest first. Per <entry>: title, link (absolute), id (same URL), updated (post date), summary (description), author. Feed-level updated = newest post's date. Gated on site.config.baseURL so it can ship dark until the host is confirmed.

nodes.label: renderReleasesAtom
nodes.doc: renderReleasesAtom writes gen/public/atom/releases.atom.xml from parsed releases (newest first as authored). Per <entry>: title = version, link = site.config.repoURL/releases/tag/<ver>, id = same, updated = release date, summary = the section body. Feed-level updated = newest release's date. Gated on site.config.baseURL and on having at least one released version.

nodes.label: abandonedLinkCheck
nodes.doc: abandonedLinkCheck is the parity gate: every URL the site has shipped before (recorded in URL_LOCK) must still resolve, so a renamed or deleted page can't silently start 404-ing on inbound links and bookmarks. To retire a URL on purpose, either add a redirect (frontmatter `aliases:`, whose stub keeps the old URL resolving) or list it in retired.urls.lock. Runs every render; the lock only grows (updateUrlLock, under the rw charm).

nodes.label: assetIntegrityCheck
nodes.doc: assetIntegrityCheck throws on any dangling href/src in the written output, so a renamed bundle or forgotten alias fails the build instead of shipping a 404.

nodes.label: axisReport
nodes.doc: axisReport lists pages reachable by fewer than three KINDS of route - tree, sequence, topic. See Site.pageAxes for why kinds rather than link count.  It REPORTS rather than throws, deliberately. orphanCheck can throw because its bar is objective: a page is reachable or it is not. "Three axes" is an editorial target, and a gate that fails the build the moment someone adds a page - before they have tagged it - trains people to reach for an escape hatch. Print the shortfall, let it be burned down, and promote

nodes.label: buildCommits
nodes.doc: buildCommits parses one git-log pass: - metaCommits: path -> "full|short|stamp" of the FIRST (newest) sighting; drives the always-visible "Last updated" footer line. - metaHistory: path -> up to HISTORY_MAX "full|short|stamp|subject" entries, newest- first; drives the collapsed history panel. The log prints "SUBJ:<subject>" after each ">>>" header so both fields ride together without a second git spawn.

nodes.label: checkPathExists
nodes.doc: checkPathExists returns true when target (gen-root-relative, no leading slash) resolves to a real file under gen/. Directory refs (URL ending in "/" or a plain slugged path) resolve to their index.html; assets pass through verbatim. fs\isFile / fs\isDir, not os\execute(["test", ...]). This is the hottest filesystem predicate in the render by a wide margin: assetIntegrityCheck calls it for EVERY href and src on every written page, and each call took up to three forks. Tens of thousands of fork+exec pairs is

nodes.label: collectFindings
nodes.doc: collectFindings runs both halves over one file into the single tier that throws.

nodes.label: collectMarkdown
nodes.doc: collectMarkdown appends every .md file under dir (recursively) to acc, as a path relative to the walk root.

nodes.label: conventionsCheck
nodes.doc: conventionsCheck holds the docs corpus to the conventions page it ships. It runs from `lint`, NOT from the render, on purpose: a prose nit must not fail `build`. A gate that fails the wrong target teaches people that the failing target is unreliable, and the next real breakage in it gets waved through.  Every finding THROWS: a `$ ` prompt in a command block, a pinned version standing in for example output, a backticked path that has since moved, and a markdown link that no longer resolves are all facts abou

nodes.label: loadMeta
nodes.doc: loadMeta populates the commit-metadata fields once, shelling out to git. The GitHub source-navigation links (edit/blame/history/blob) use the git symbolic ref HEAD, which GitHub resolves to the repo's default branch: honest (it names the canonical line, not a fabricated branch), rename-proof (survives a default-branch rename), and identical on every branch so a feature-branch render never drifts - the reason the old hardcoded "main" existed, now solved without the lie.

nodes.label: orphanCheck
nodes.doc: orphanCheck proves every docs page is reachable by BFS from the nav roots, so a page with no inbound link fails the build instead of shipping unreachable.

nodes.label: pageKey
nodes.doc: pageKey normalizes a scanReferencesInHTML result (a gen-root-relative path with no trailing slash - "spells/go", "index.html", "assets/x.png") to a page key: "" for the home page, else the directory that holds the page's index.html. Asset paths pass through unchanged and simply never match a real page key.

nodes.label: pathExists
nodes.doc: pathExists is the one filesystem question the conventions lint asks.

nodes.label: pruneStaleOutputs
nodes.doc: pruneStaleOutputs deletes gen/ output whose source no longer produces it - a renamed/removed page, a deleted post, a dropped alias, a release out of CHANGELOG.md. gen/ is not wiped before each render, so this keeps it from accumulating orphans: for every "<dir>/index.html" not in writtenPaths and not in alwaysKeep, delete the whole directory (sibling index.md and all). Runs before assetIntegrityCheck/orphanCheck so neither trips on a stale page's dangling reference to content removed with it.

nodes.label: readURLSet
nodes.doc: readURLSet reads a newline-delimited URL file into a set, skipping blanks and "#" comments. Missing file -> empty set (the bootstrap case for URL_LOCK).

nodes.label: scanReferencesInHTML
nodes.doc: scanReferencesInHTML pulls every href="..." and src="..." out of html, skipping external URLs, mailto:, javascript:, data:, and pure fragments. Each reference is returned as a gen-root-relative path (resolved against pageDir).

nodes.label: updateUrlLock
nodes.doc: updateUrlLock folds this build's URLs into URL_LOCK and rewrites it sorted. It only adds - a URL that drops out of the build stays in the ledger so the gate keeps demanding a redirect or an explicit retirement for it. Called under the rw charm so a plain (checking) render never mutates the tree.

nodes.label: walkGen
nodes.doc: walkGen recursively enumerates every written file under gen/ so the integrity check reads each once.

nodes.label: writeSiteManifest
nodes.doc: writeSiteManifest emits gen/site-manifest.sha256: one "<sha256>  <path>\n" line (standard sha256sum(1) format, so `sha256sum -c` verifies it directly) per file shipped under gen/, repo-relative, sorted. Called from generate() AFTER generateJsBundles(), not from site_render(), because generateJsBundles() writes gen/assets/hljs.js (served assets) only after site_render() returns - computing the manifest earlier would omit them. Excludes its own output path (a file cannot hash itself).

nodes.label: deriveDescription
nodes.doc: deriveDescription is the fallback page description: the first substantive paragraph of the rendered HTML, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed, entities decoded, truncated on a word boundary. A leading image-only paragraph (the hero) is skipped. "" when no paragraph has text, so the caller can fall back to site.config.description. Decoding here (before escapeAttr re-encodes) avoids double-encoding.

nodes.label: deriveTitle
nodes.doc: deriveTitle reads the title from the first H1, stripping backticks (a heading like `# `fs``) so it reads as plain text in <title>, breadcrumb, pager, and search index. Frontmatter titles bypass this and are used verbatim.

nodes.label: generatedFrom
nodes.doc: generatedFrom reads the frontmatter `generated_from:` value (empty when absent, which means the page is hand-written). A repo-relative path or comma-joined glob list names the source directly; a value ending in "/" is an in-site path to the section overview that carries the real source link(s) instead - see internal/docs.Frontmatter.

nodes.label: insertSinceBadge
nodes.doc: insertSinceBadge places an "Added in <version>" marker under the H1 so a reader can tell whether a feature exists in their installed magus. magus follows Go-style compatibility (no v2), so one page serves every version and just notes when a thing arrived. since is the frontmatter `since:` value; no-op without a `since:` or an H1 to anchor to.

nodes.label: insertSizeRatio
nodes.doc: insertSizeRatio places a size comparison under the H1 of an agent-skill page: how much smaller the `--simple` permutation is, as a number and as a bar.  The bar is a bare `<progress>`. Pico styles that element classlessly (`progress{accent-color:var(--pico-primary)}` plus a themed track in both color schemes), so the ratio gets a graphic with no custom CSS and no new markup vocabulary - which is the site's whole rule. It is also the semantically correct element: a proportion of a known whole, readable by a

nodes.label: pageType
nodes.doc: pageType reads the frontmatter `page_type:` marker (empty when absent). The value that matters is "overview": a landing/index page that orients and routes to others. Related ranking favors these hubs and the reachability gate trusts them as roots, so declaring the type in frontmatter beats guessing it from a URL shape.

nodes.label: parseTags
nodes.doc: parseTags reads the frontmatter `tags:` list as [str] (empty when absent). The one extraction point, so rendered chips and the search index draw from the same source.

nodes.label: readingTime
nodes.doc: readingTime estimates minutes-to-read by weighting content by type, not raw word count: prose at 220 wpm, code counted by line (read deliberately, not skimmed), images costing a few seconds each - so a code- or figure-heavy page gets a truer number. Frontmatter is stripped so YAML doesn't skew it. "" for pages too short to label. Deterministic.

nodes.label: conventionAnchorsIn
nodes.doc: conventionAnchorsIn returns the convention sections this page can actually send a reader to, read off the hints injectConventionHints already placed in the content.  Reading the INJECTED markup rather than re-deriving which markers the page has is what keeps the two from drifting: whatever the hints link to is exactly what the drawer carries, by construction, so adding a fourth hint kind needs no change here.

nodes.label: keepConventionSections
nodes.doc: keepConventionSections is keepGlossarySections one heading level up: the conventions page is H2 sections where the glossary is H3 entries, so a section runs from its own <h2 id="> to the next one. Order is preserved.

nodes.label: keepGlossarySections
nodes.doc: keepGlossarySections keeps only the <h3 id="..."> term blocks whose anchor is in keep, in document order, and drops everything else. Same scan injectBacklinks uses: a term block runs from its own <h3 id="> to the next <h3 id="> or <h2>.

nodes.label: refDocHtml
nodes.doc: refDocHtml renders one docs/*.md to content HTML and templatizes its root-relative links.

nodes.label: renderAnnouncementBar
nodes.doc: renderAnnouncementBar renders a dismissible strip announcing the newest shipped release, or "" when none has shipped. The version comes from loadReleases (releases/*.yaml), so it is drift-stable; announcement.js hides it once the reader dismisses that version and re-shows it on the next release.  Takes root (the relative-depth prefix) like every other chrome renderer, because the optional second link points at a post on this site. The release link stays an absolute GitHub URL, so the bar needed no depth unt

nodes.label: renderCommitFooter
nodes.doc: Footer crediting the last commit that touched a page's source, falling back to HEAD for a not-yet-committed file. Keying off the file's own history means a page changes when its source does, not when any commit lands. renderCommitFooter builds the provenance strip for one page, keyed to the commit that last changed THAT PAGE's content - never to HEAD.  The HEAD fallback this replaced was the single largest source of generated-docs churn: 132 of 163 pages have no hand-written source under docs/ (the diagnost

nodes.label: renderReferenceDrawer
nodes.doc: renderReferenceDrawer shows the page ITS vocabulary, not the whole glossary.  The drawer used to inline all 47 terms on every page, identically. A reference panel that is the same everywhere answers no question you had on the page you are reading - it is a second copy of /glossary/ that happens to slide out. Scoping it to the terms this page actually uses is what makes opening it worth doing.  pageTerms is the forward-built map (see Site): it is complete before the walk starts, so the first page rendered ge

nodes.label: renderSettingsPanel
nodes.doc: renderSettingsPanel renders the gear button and its dropdown, the rightmost control in every top bar. The theme (auto/light/dark) cycle lives here on EVERY page. showConsole adds the daemon-app operator prefs (refresh rate, daemon host) that only the console apps read; docs, playground, 404, and offline get the theme row alone. console-settings.js opens/closes the panel and persists poll/host; theme.js drives #theme-cycle (it owns the pre-paint theme set()). Both scripts no-op when their controls are absent

nodes.label: renderSiteFooter
nodes.doc: renderSiteFooter renders the shared one-line attribution footer: root-relative site links (Search, /public/ files) reachable from every page, then absolute GitHub/Buzz links. The License link points at the pinned site.metaBranch. root is the prefix back to gen/'s root, so the site links resolve at any depth.

nodes.label: renderSiteNav
nodes.doc: renderSiteNav renders the shared top bar (brand + section links + settings gear). One definition for every page, so adding a nav item lands everywhere at once. root is the prefix back to gen/'s root; active is the current section's key (or ""). withRef shows the Reference drawer trigger only where the page ships #ref-drawer + ref-drawer.js and loads console.css (which sizes the icon button): the docs and playground. The 404 and offline pages have no reference content, so they pass false to omit the button.

nodes.label: renderTocList
nodes.doc: renderTocList builds the "On this page" block from a page's h2/h3 headings (goldmark puts each on its own line with a slug id); h3s nest under their h2. Returns "" below three headings - too little for a sidebar. Returns just the title + list; renderPage() wraps it in the .toc <aside>, and toc.js adds scroll-spy + the collapse toggle.

nodes.label: diagramDrift
nodes.doc: diagramDrift re-exports the anchor check, alongside writeDiagramPair.

nodes.label: injectDemoCallout
nodes.doc:
injectDemoCallout inserts the "Interactive demo" callout after a page's intro (the first

), deep-linking href (a tour card). A distinct component (its own teal identity), not a link or a button - it signals "there is a runnable demonstration of this concept."

nodes.label: pageOrder
nodes.doc: pageOrder reads one sibling's frontmatter `order:`. Orders start at 1; absent reads as 0 from .integer(), which is why 0 counts as unordered rather than first.

nodes.label: render404
nodes.doc: render404 writes gen/404.html - the themed page GitHub Pages serves for any unmatched path. GH Pages keeps the deep 404 URL in the address bar, so ordinary relative paths would break; this page uses root-absolute paths (/<basePath>/site.css, etc.) - the one deliberate exception to the relative-link scheme. basePath comes from site.config.baseURL (https://eli.gladman.cc/magus/ -> "/magus/"), falling back to "/" when empty so the page still renders locally from the server root.

nodes.label: renderFile
nodes.doc: Render one docs/*.md file to a sibling *.html under gen. rel is relative to the docs/ subtree; srcRel (site.docs/rel) is magus/-relative for the footer/edit link.

nodes.label: renderGeneratedChips
nodes.doc: renderGeneratedChips renders a generated page's provenance as two chips: the existing "generated" status chip, then a link chip naming the source it came from.  They stay SEPARATE rather than merging into one linked status chip, because the two styles say different things and the CSS already encodes that: .tag.generated is filled with cursor:help to read as a status (see site.css), while .post-tags a.tag is outlined and fills on hover to read as interactive. A filled chip that is also a link gets no visible

nodes.label: renderPager
nodes.doc: renderPager builds the prev/next links among a page's siblings - the other rendered docs in the same source directory (README/index and underscore fixtures excluded). "" when there is no sibling on either side. rel is docs-relative (e.g. "modules/fs.md").  Ordered by frontmatter `order:`, falling back to filename. Filename order alone was an accident presented as a sequence: on concepts/targets.md it produced "Previous: Spells, Next: Telemetry" purely because s < t < t, implying a reading path that did not

nodes.label: renderPagerLink
nodes.doc: renderPagerLink renders one prev/next card, reading the sibling's source so it credits the same title (frontmatter title, else first H1) the sibling page renders with.

nodes.label: renderRoot
nodes.doc: Render the repo's top-level README.md as the /development/ landing (README_URL). It is the same document GitHub shows on the repository front page - the full pitch, the architecture, and how to build and test the tree - so it is the contributor section's overview rather than the site's front door; site/landing.buzz owns gen/index.html.  Links like href="docs/X" are repo-root-relative, which is what GitHub needs. From gen/development/index.html the docs tree is one level up, so the prefix is rewritten to "..

nodes.label: repoBlobHref
nodes.doc: srcRel is the page's source path relative to magus/ (e.g. "docs/spells.md"), driving the commit footer and "Suggest an edit" link. description is resolved (frontmatter, else derived, else site default), always non-empty so the meta tag fires. canonUrl is the clean gen-root URL ("" for home). pager is the prev/next nav (may be ""). repoBlobHref resolves a repo-relative path or glob to a GitHub blob URL. GitHub does not resolve glob syntax as a URL, so a glob ("std/**/*.go") links the directory before its fir

nodes.label: substituteVersionTokens
nodes.doc: substituteVersionTokens swaps __MAGUS_VERSION__ for the latest release version WITH the leading "v" (e.g. "v0.1.0"), read from releases/*.yaml via loadReleases - the single source of truth (do NOT read git tags). Run before render AND before the md is written back as index.md, so the page and its "View source" copy agree. No-op when no release has shipped (the token stays literal, prompting a cut).

nodes.label: writeDiagramPair
nodes.doc: writeDiagramPair re-exports the standalone writer so the magusfile can reach it through render.buzz. It lives behind this module because the registry may have exactly one importer, and the site render is the consumer that cannot give it up.

nodes.label: writeOffline
nodes.doc: writeOffline writes gen/offline/index.html - shown by the service worker when a navigation fails (network down, no cached copy). Like render404 it uses root-absolute asset paths, since its URL depth differs from the rest of the site. Playground is called out because it is precached and fully functional offline.

nodes.label: isDirectory
nodes.doc: True if path is a directory.  fs\isDir, not os\execute(["test", "-d", ...]): the shell-out forked and exec'd a process PER CHECK, and this is called for every entry of every tree walk - the page walk, the doc-page collection, the glossary pass, the code-entity pass. A stat syscall is roughly a thousand times cheaper than a fork+exec, and the render was spending more time in the kernel than in the interpreter because of it.

nodes.label: isGeneratorDir
nodes.doc: isGeneratorDir reports whether a docs-ROOT child directory is the SSG's own rather than content. The SSG sits co-located with its markdown, so the content walk shares a tree with node_modules/, gen/, src/, and tour/, whose stray .md (package READMEs, generated index.md) must not be ingested as pages. CRUCIAL: call sites guard on rel == "", so only EXACT docs-root children are skipped - a content subdir sharing one of these names at any depth is still walked.

nodes.label: isGeneratorFile
nodes.doc: isGeneratorFile reports whether a docs-ROOT .md file is an SSG artifact rather than content. MAGUS.md (the generated target catalog) sits at the docs root but must not render as a doc page; it surfaces instead via renderDevelopment. Like isGeneratorDir, consulted only at the docs root (rel == "").

nodes.label: isNeverContentDir
nodes.doc: isNeverContentDir reports whether a directory can never hold site content, at ANY depth - as opposed to isGeneratorDir above, which is deliberately root-only.  node_modules is the whole list. A package tree holds thousands of README.md files and none of them are this site's pages. The root-only rule covered docs/node_modules but not a nested one, so the moment a sub-project under docs/ had its dependencies installed - which `magus run ci docs/guides/integrations/agents` does - the walk started rendering eve

nodes.label: makeOutputDir
nodes.doc: makeOutputDir creates a written page's output directory, naming the conflict when a FILE already occupies that path.  gen/ is not a pure render target: committed static files live in it alongside generated pages. gen/install is the install script the README's curl one-liner fetches, and pruneStaleOutputs lists it under alwaysKeep for exactly that reason. A page whose clean URL is /install/ therefore needs gen/install to be a directory, which it can never be.  Without this guard the render dies inside the mk

nodes.label: buildServiceWorker
nodes.doc: buildServiceWorker bundles src/site/service-worker.ts to gen/service-worker.js with esbuild, injecting the cache version and precache list via --define. The version is a digest of the precached assets' own digests, so it changes exactly when a cached asset does (and is byte-stable otherwise) - and that byte change is the signal a browser uses to fetch the new worker.

nodes.label: writeManifest
nodes.doc: writeManifest writes gen/manifest.webmanifest - the PWA metadata browsers read to allow "install this site". scope/start_url match the deploy base so a nested install stays inside /magus/. Gated on baseURL so the scope is well-defined; without it we'd default to "/" and mis-scope.

nodes.label: climb
nodes.doc: climb builds n repetitions of "../".

nodes.label: climbFromDir
nodes.doc: climbFromDir returns the "../" prefix from a gen-relative directory back to gen's root, one "../" per segment ("console/dashboard" -> "../../"). App pages derive their nav prefix from their output location so it can't drift from the write path.

nodes.label: newCleanDirectory
nodes.doc: newCleanDirectory gives a docs page's clean directory (its clean URL minus the trailing slash), the "new dir" arg the link rewriter needs. Reads site state (blog dir via cleanURL), so it lives here; the pure oldFlatDirectory counterpart is in lib/html.

nodes.label: rootPrefix
nodes.doc: rootPrefix returns the relative path from a page back up to gen/'s root ("" for spells.html, "../../" for codes/sandbox/X.html), so shared nav and theme.js resolve at any page depth and the site works under a project subpath.

nodes.label: sitePathPrefix
nodes.doc: sitePathPrefix returns the root-absolute URL path prefix: the path component of baseURL ("https://host/magus/" -> "/magus/"), or "/" when baseURL is unset. Used only where depth is unpredictable (404, SW offline fallback, PWA manifest/worker); other pages use the depth-relative rootPrefix. One definition so the derivation isn't copy-pasted.

nodes.label: renderSyntaxRow
nodes.doc: renderSearchPage writes gen/search/index.html: the deep-linkable search surface. A tool page (no markdown source; kept out of the search index, sitemap, and provenance chrome via renderPage()'s srcRel guards). The #search-page container is the signal search.js keys off to switch from the header dropdown to full-page, URL-synced (?q=) results. renderSyntaxRow renders one Search Syntax entry: a clickable example that runs itself (search.js intercepts the ?q= link) beside a plain-language description. The quer

nodes.label: ci
nodes.doc: 'ci' is the anchor `magus affected ci` keys off. There is nothing to build here, so the gate is lint plus the plugin's transport tests. The rest of what these files must agree WITH is checked at the repo root: dogfood_test.go verifies that this repository's own hook config invokes them, that the guide embeds them verbatim, and that each declares a stance for every decision and surface in the guard contract (the magus-guard-coverage lines).  This comment used to claim the templates' behavior was asserted fro

nodes.label: format
nodes.doc: format owns the Markdown in this directory - the per-host guide pages beside the templates. The docs project cannot do it: dprint discovers this project's dprint.json and would format the subtree under it, which is a parent target writing into a descendant project (MGS3001). So the pages are formatted by the project that owns them, which is the same rule every other project with Markdown follows.

nodes.label: install
nodes.doc: pnpm, NOT npm: .npmrc's minimum-release-age supply-chain gate is the reason. Always let pnpm validate the install. An interrupted install leaves a node_modules that EXISTS but is incomplete, and the isDir guard this replaced read that as ready, handing the missing packages straight to tsc/esbuild. Reached once per invocation through preflight, which every target below already needs, so the unconditional --frozen-lockfile costs about a second on a warm tree and never races itself.

nodes.label: lint
nodes.doc: lint is the templates' static-analysis gate: the TypeScript type-check (tsc --noEmit) plus Biome's banned patterns (no `any`, no non-null assertions - see biome.json, which mirrors libs/textsearch's rules so the whole workspace writes TypeScript the same way). proc.exec raises on a non-zero exit, so either gate fails lint.

nodes.label: test
nodes.doc: test runs the OpenCode plugin's transport cases: does it ASK magus correctly (the top-level `hook` subcommand, the input on stdin) and handle each decision the way it declares.  It runs under node, not bun, even though the plugin's runtime is bun. The test supplies Bun.spawn - the only Bun API the plugin touches - and leaves the shipped artifact unmodified, which is a better trade than putting a second JS runtime in every contributor's toolchain for one file. The residual gap is bun-versus-node spawn semant

nodes.label: cleanConventionDef
nodes.doc: cleanConventionDef reduces a section's lead paragraph to a short plain-text blurb: drop backticks and bold markers, and a trailing colon.

nodes.label: closesFence
nodes.doc: closesFence reports whether the line is a closing fence for an open marker: the same character, at least as long, and nothing else on the line.

nodes.label: fenceLang
nodes.doc: fenceLang is the first word of the info string after the opening marker, lowercased.

nodes.label: fenceMarker
nodes.doc: fenceMarker returns the fence marker a line opens with, or "". CommonMark counts the marker's LENGTH, which is what lets a four-backtick fence hold three-backtick fences inside it - the conventions page does exactly that to show how a runnable block is authored, and a naive toggle would read the inner fence as a close and mis-attribute every rule after it.

nodes.label: fileDir
nodes.doc: fileDir returns the directory portion of a repo-root-relative file path (splitPath drops "" and "." segments), so a relative link target can be resolved against it.

nodes.label: injectConventionHints
nodes.doc:
injectConventionHints adds a "?" hint into each rendered convention marker: an admonition title and a code-block caption. It runs after the content transforms, so it sees the final

/

nodes.label: injectFirstPlaceholderHint
nodes.doc: injectFirstPlaceholderHint appends a "?" hint after the FIRST inline <code> on the page that holds an angle-bracket placeholder (<...>), linking to the placeholders convention. First occurrence only - like the glossary linker - so a page that uses the syntax gets one quiet hint, never one per placeholder. Inline code is told from a fenced block by having no newline, so a multi-line code block is never hinted.

nodes.label: insertBeforeClose
nodes.doc: insertBeforeClose inserts `ins` just before the first `close` following each `open` marker. Returns html unchanged when ins is "" (the section was not in the corpus).

nodes.label: isCommentLine
nodes.doc: isCommentLine reports whether a line inside a fence is a comment - the form the docs use to show a command's expected output.

nodes.label: isDigit
nodes.doc: isDigit reports whether byte b is ASCII 0-9.

nodes.label: linkTargets
nodes.doc: linkTargets returns every `](target)` markdown-link target on a line, in order. A link with no closing paren on the line is dropped rather than guessed at.

nodes.label: lintMarkdown
nodes.doc: lintMarkdown checks one page against the conventions it can be checked against, and returns every violation rather than the first: a run that reports one nit per invocation trains people to fix one thing and re-run, which is the slowest possible loop.

nodes.label: looksLikeRepoPath
nodes.doc: looksLikeRepoPath reports whether an inline-code token is claiming a file in THIS repository. The bar is deliberately high, and it was raised by running the rule over the corpus: the first draft produced 67 hits of which about eight were real. Everything the exclusions below remove is a path this repo legitimately writes about without owning - a reader's own workspace, their home directory, a cache tree that only exists at runtime.  Two limits are worth knowing, because they are the price of a quiet rule:

nodes.label: namesPinnedVersion
nodes.doc: namesPinnedVersion reports whether s pins a magus version literally - "magus 0.4.2", "magus v0.4.2". Sample output in the docs is supposed to show the SHAPE of what a command prints, because a pasted-in version goes stale the next release and nothing notices. This is the rule that caught `# magus 0.4.2` under "Shell commands", which was two releases behind AND the wrong format.

nodes.label: parseConventions
nodes.doc: parseConventions reads conventions.md into its sections: each "## Heading" becomes a Convention with its anchor and the paragraph under it (markup stripped, trailing colon dropped since a lead line often ends in ":" before an example).

nodes.label: pathCheckApplies
nodes.doc: pathCheckApplies reports whether a page's inline paths and link targets are claims about THIS repository. The diagnostic explainers under reference/codes/ are exempt because their whole job is describing someone else's workspace (`api/`, `pkg/build.go`). Measuring the old blanket docs/guides/ exemption against the corpus found exactly one guide that needs it: pr-advice.md names `refs/remotes/`, a git-internal path inside the READER's own clone, not a claim about this repository. Every other guide's inline p

nodes.label: pathReferences
nodes.doc: pathReferences collects every repo path named in inline code OUTSIDE a fenced block, and every relative markdown link target, with the line each sits on. Prose is where a path claim is load-bearing - a reader follows it - whereas a path inside a command block is often illustrative, so scanning only prose keeps this honest without keeping it noisy. A link target is resolved against its own file's directory, so `f.path` is repo-root relative for both kinds of finding, like the caller already expects.  The cal

nodes.label: relativeMarkdownLinkBody
nodes.doc: relativeMarkdownLinkBody reports the target's path with any "#fragment" stripped, or null if the target is not a same-repo relative .md claim: an anchor-only target, an http(s) or mailto URL, and a site-absolute link (leading "/") are not filesystem references.

nodes.label: runOf
nodes.doc: runOf returns the leading run of byte `ch` in s ("```buzz" -> "```").

nodes.label: computeCSP
nodes.doc: computeCSP builds one page's Content-Security-Policy meta content (see Site.csp/ Site.cspBadges for which pages get which img-src). default-src is 'self', not 'none': manifest-src, the same-origin <link rel=prefetch> hover-warm, and the service worker registration all fall back to default-src (via worker-src -> child-src), and 'none' would break the service worker outright. 'self' is the minimal fallback that keeps them working without opening any directive wider than same-origin. Every directive the site n

nodes.label: cspForRedirectStub
nodes.doc: cspForRedirectStub builds the CSP a plain alias redirect page needs - distinct from the site-wide policy because a stub (aliasStub) loads no stylesheet, image, or external script; its only content is one inline <script> that differs per stub, so it cannot share the site-wide hash list. script is the exact text redirectScript(rel) (lib/html.buzz) produces, so the hash always matches what ships.

nodes.label: extractInlineScripts
nodes.doc: extractInlineScripts pulls the text of every attribute-less `<script>...</script>` block out of html, in order. Matches only the literal "<script>" open tag: a `<script src=...>` is an external load already covered by script-src 'self', not a hash-source candidate.

nodes.label: fileSha256
nodes.doc: fileSha256 reads path and returns its lowercase-hex SHA-256 digest. Single place file bytes get hashed (writeServiceWorker's cache-version stamp and writeSiteManifest's per-asset integrity list), so the two never compute "the same hash" two different ways.

nodes.label: scriptHash
nodes.doc: scriptHash returns a CSP `sha256-<base64>` source for js's exact text (the same bytes a browser hashes against a hash-source script-src). crypto.hash returns raw digest bytes, so .hex() renders the lowercase hex this decodes; CSP hash-sources are base64, so hexDecode back to raw digest bytes before base64-encoding.

nodes.label: blogDate
nodes.doc: blogDate renders a post's frontmatter date as a plain calendar byline ("July 1, 2026").

nodes.label: blogDateAttr
nodes.doc: blogDateAttr is the date-only "YYYY-MM-DD" that pairs with blogDate() in <time datetime>.

nodes.label: formatISO
nodes.doc: formatISO renders an ISO 8601 UTC string as "June 29, 2026, 1:41 AM UTC" (no-JS fallback; client JS rewrites it to the viewer's local zone).

nodes.label: formatISOShort
nodes.doc: formatISOShort is the compact recent-changes form ("Jan 2, 2006").

nodes.label: isFuturePost
nodes.doc: isFuturePost reports whether date falls on a UTC day after asOf's. Same day is not future: a post dated the day of the build publishes that day. An undated post never is.  asOf is site.metaStamp (HEAD's commit date), never wall-clock: generate is a drift gate, so the render stays a pure function of the tree rather than of when it ran. Empty asOf fails open, since a missing git stamp should not blank every dated post.

nodes.label: attr
nodes.doc: attr renders one escaped attribute with a leading space: ` name="value"`.

nodes.label: el
nodes.doc: el wraps raw body in <tag attrs>...</tag>. attrs is "" or a run of attr() calls.

nodes.label: esc
nodes.doc: esc escapes text for HTML element content (& < >).

nodes.label: voidEl
nodes.doc: voidEl is an unclosed element: <tag attrs> (meta, link, img).

nodes.label: atomDate
nodes.doc: atomDate normalizes a frontmatter date to RFC3339 UTC (bare date -> T00:00:00Z).

nodes.label: escapeXml
nodes.doc: escapeXml is escapeAttr's XML form: five entities, ampersand FIRST so the & each of the other four introduces is never rescanned. (This note used to say "& last", which is the opposite of both the code and the correct order - replacing it last would turn "<" into "&lt;".)

nodes.label: xmlAttribute
nodes.doc: Minimal XML leaves; every body and value funnels through escapeXml. Container tags with their own namespaces (<feed>, <urlset>, <entry>, <url>) stay written inline.

nodes.label: acceptable
nodes.doc: acceptable reports whether needle matched at pos (length n) in searchable is a whole word (non-word boundaries) that does not overlap an already-placed insertion.

nodes.label: cleanConfigCell
nodes.doc: cleanConfigCell trims a markdown table cell and drops its backticks (env-var underscores are kept - they are part of the name, not markdown).

nodes.label: cleanDef
nodes.doc: cleanDef reduces a glossary definition paragraph to a short plain-text blurb for the popover: cut the trailing "See ..." cross-link, unwrap [text](url) to text, drop backticks.

nodes.label: glossarySlug
nodes.doc: glossarySlug mirrors goldmark's heading-id slug: lowercase, spaces AND underscores to hyphens, drop any char that is not a-z, 0-9, or hyphen. "Output reference" -> "output-reference"; "MAGUS.md" -> "magusmd"; "write_file" -> "write-file".

nodes.label: hasNoLinkAttr
nodes.doc: Both maskers key off the tag NAME, so a <span> reads as prose no matter what it holds. That split "magusfile.buzz" in a code panel's title bar into two popovers, one on "magusfile" and one on "buzz", because neither linker has a term for the filename and both had a term for its halves. data-nolink marks an element whose text is a literal - a filename, a command line - rather than prose to be read.

nodes.label: injectBacklinks
nodes.doc: injectBacklinks appends each term's "referenced on" fragment (byAnchor[anchor], a caller-built HTML string) at the END of that term's section on the glossary page - just before the next <h3>/<h2> heading, so it sits below the definition. The glossary is rendered after the full walk, so byAnchor holds the complete cross-reference set. Pure string surgery; anchors with no fragment are left untouched.

nodes.label: isSkipContainer
nodes.doc: isSkipContainer is true for tags whose text content must never be auto-linked: pre (fenced code always), a (no nested links), and headings. Inline <code> is skipped only in prose mode (glossary terms) - code entities (MGSxxxx codes, commands, mod\method) DELIBERATELY link inside inline code, which is where those references appear.

nodes.label: linkCodeEntities
nodes.doc: linkCodeEntities links the first occurrence of each entity's match string (inside inline code or prose, never a fenced <pre> block) to its reference page, baking the summary into data-def and the kind into data-kind for the shared popover (glossary-terms.js). entities MUST be longest-match-first; pageDir is the linking page's clean gen-root dir (for the href).

nodes.label: linkGlossaryTerms
nodes.doc: linkGlossaryTerms links the first linkable occurrence of each term (terms MUST be ordered longest-first so multi-word terms win over their substrings) to relToGlossary + "#" + anchor, and records which anchors were linked. A page carrying the "<!-- magus-noglossary -->" opt-out marker is returned verbatim (marker stripped) with nothing linked.

nodes.label: lowerByte
nodes.doc: lowerByte lowercases an ASCII byte (A-Z -> a-z), leaving others untouched. Used to compare bytes case-insensitively WITHOUT allocating a lowercased substring per position - the hot path here runs over every character of every page for every term, so allocation-free byte comparison is what keeps a full-site render fast.

nodes.label: maskLinkable
nodes.doc: maskLinkable returns html the SAME LENGTH, with every byte outside linkable text replaced by a space and the linkable text lowercased. Non-linkable = inside a tag (< .. >), an HTML comment, or a skip container (pre/a/headings, plus inline code when skipInlineCode). A native indexOf then lands only in linkable text, so the ONE interpreted pass over the page is this build - not one scan per term, which is the difference between a fast render and a ten-minute one. Emits per-run pieces (not per char) so allocat

nodes.label: parseConfigRow
nodes.doc: parseConfigRow parses a config.md table row "| `key` | `ENV` | `--flag` | type |" into a dotted config key and a one-line popover summary (its type, how to set it via flag/env). Returns ok=false for the header, the separator, and any non-dotted key.

nodes.label: parseGlossary
nodes.doc: parseGlossary reads the glossary Markdown into terms: each "### Term" H3 becomes a GlossaryTerm with its goldmark anchor and a one-line definition (the paragraph under the heading, cross-link and markup stripped). Returned longest-first for matching.

nodes.label: requireIndexOfFrom
nodes.doc: applyLinks wraps the first acceptable occurrence of each token (tokens/opens/keys are parallel and longest-first) in open ... , matching natively on the masked `searchable` and inserting into html right-to-left so earlier positions never shift. Returns the linked html and the keys linked (longest-first). If masking changed the length (a non-ASCII case fold, not expected in these docs), it returns html unlinked rather than misplace a link. requireIndexOfFrom fails fast when the running magus predates str

nodes.label: scanPast
nodes.doc: scanPast returns the index just past the next occurrence of s at/after `from`, or the end of html. Allocation-free replacement for html.sub(from).indexOf(s) + s.len().

nodes.label: scanPastByte
nodes.doc: scanPastByte returns the index just past the next `target` byte at/after `from`, or the end of html. An allocation-free replacement for html.sub(from).indexOf(<char>) + 1.

nodes.label: sortEntitiesLongestFirst
nodes.doc: sortEntitiesLongestFirst orders entities by descending match length, so linkCodeEntities tries "magus affected ci" before "magus affected". Selection sort; the catalogs are small.

nodes.label: sortLongestFirst
nodes.doc: sortLongestFirst returns terms ordered by descending term length, so linkGlossaryTerms matches a multi-word term before any of its substring terms. Selection sort; the term set is small (a few dozen).

nodes.label: spaces
nodes.doc: spaces returns n space bytes, built by doubling (O(log n) concats) so masking a large protected region stays cheap.

nodes.label: tagNameLower
nodes.doc: tagNameLower reads the tag name at a '<' (skipping a leading '/'), lowercased.

nodes.label: unwrapLinks
nodes.doc: unwrapLinks turns each markdown "[text](url)" into just "text".

nodes.label: aliasStub
nodes.doc: aliasStub is the redirect page written at each alias: meta-refresh + canonical + scripted replace + a plain <a>, so it works with or without JavaScript. csp is the caller-computed policy (cspForRedirectStub, hashing redirectScript(rel) - the page's only content, so default-src 'none' plus that one script hash suffices).

nodes.label: cleanBody
nodes.doc: cleanBody reduces a raw markdown body to compact prose for the search index: drop fenced blocks, strip a few inline markers, collapse whitespace.

nodes.label: cleanTarget
nodes.doc: cleanTarget maps a flat gen-root path to its clean URL: drop .html, drop a trailing index/README landing, add a trailing slash.

nodes.label: externalLinks
nodes.doc: externalLinks adds rel/target/data-external to every http(s) anchor that lacks them.

nodes.label: lazyImages
nodes.doc: lazyImages adds loading="lazy" decoding="async" to every without a loading or fetchpriority attribute (author markup wins, so the hero stays eager).

nodes.label: oldFlatDirectory
nodes.doc: oldFlatDirectory is a docs page's pre-move directory (its source subdir).

nodes.label: redirectScript
nodes.doc: redirectScript is the exact inline-script body aliasStub emits below. Exposed so writeAliases computes the stub's CSP sha256-hash from the SAME text; hashing a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift the moment either side changes.

nodes.label: renderContentHTML
nodes.doc: renderContentHTML is the one post-processing pipeline every page runs: rewrite links (href AND path-named link text), then the ordered content transforms. One choke point so no transform gets applied on one path and forgotten on another.

nodes.label: resolvePath
nodes.doc: resolvePath resolves a relative link against a gen-root-relative dir, normalizing ".." and dropping "." / empty segments ("" for the root).

nodes.label: rewriteHref
nodes.doc: rewriteHref rebases one in-content link: resolve against the old flat dir, map to the new clean URL, re-relativize to the new dir. External/anchor/mailto pass through; #fragment preserved; asset (non-.html) links re-based but not cleaned.

nodes.label: rewriteLinks
nodes.doc: rewriteLinks applies rewriteHref to every href="..." in a rendered fragment.

nodes.label: stripMdFromLinkText
nodes.doc: stripMdFromLinkText drops a trailing ".md" from LINK TEXT (between > and ). rewriteLinks cleans the href, but a path-named link (e.g. [workspace.md](workspace.md), common in the glossary) still shows a stale ".md". Only ".md" immediately before is touched, so bare path-named links are hit and other link text left alone.

nodes.label: tagAdmonition
nodes.doc:
tagAdmonition turns GitHub-alert blockquotes ("
\n

[!TYPE]\n...") into

callouts. Unknown types pass through.

nodes.label: tagRunnable
nodes.doc: tagRunnable swaps the <pre> after a "<!-- magus-run -->" / "<!-- magus-run-recorder -->" marker with a data-magus-run <pre> so run-example.js can find opt-in blocks; drops the marker. Every magus-authored doc marker shares the "magus-" prefix (and mirrors to a "data-magus-" attribute) so generated hooks are obviously ours.

nodes.label: tagRunnableMarker
nodes.doc: tagRunnableMarker replaces the <pre> following each marker with openTag; a marker not immediately before a fence is just dropped.

nodes.label: tagVersionNote
nodes.doc: tagCodeTitle wraps the <pre> after a "<!-- magus-code-title: NAME -->" marker in a <figure class="code-block-titled"> with a <figcaption>; drops the marker. tagVersionNote turns "<!-- magus-since: v0.4.0 -->" and "<!-- magus-changed: v0.4.0 -->" into the same chip the frontmatter `since:` badge renders, so one convention covers both.  SECTION level, deliberately, where the frontmatter badge is PAGE level. concepts/targets.md long predates the release that changed one behavior inside it, so a page badge read

nodes.label: wrapTables
nodes.doc: wrapTables wraps each <table> in a <figure class="table-scroll"> so a wide table scrolls horizontally instead of overflowing on narrow screens. goldmark emits a bare <table> that Pico renders full-bleed with no overflow handling.

nodes.label: capitalizeFirst
nodes.doc: capitalizeFirst upper-cases the first character of a slug (a breadcrumb label).

nodes.label: collapseWs
nodes.doc: collapseWs folds any whitespace run into a single space, so a derived description reads as one clean line.

nodes.label: decodeEntities
nodes.doc: decodeEntities turns HTML entities back into characters for a plain-text description. & decodes LAST so "&lt;" is not double-decoded into "<".

nodes.label: escapeAttr
nodes.doc: escapeAttr makes s safe inside a double-quoted HTML attribute.

nodes.label: firstPathSegment
nodes.doc: firstPathSegment returns the leading segment of a clean URL ("spells/go/" -> "spells").

nodes.label: pad4
nodes.doc: pad4 zero-pads a small non-negative int to four digits so scores sort lexically.

nodes.label: relativePath
nodes.doc: relativePath returns the path from fromDir to toUrl. Trailing slash on toUrl means it is a directory; "./" when they resolve to the same place.

nodes.label: sharedTagCount
nodes.doc: sharedTagCount counts tags common to two ||-joined tag strings (relatedness signal).

nodes.label: splitPath
nodes.doc: splitPath splits a gen-root-relative path into non-empty segments, dropping ".".

nodes.label: strLess
nodes.doc: strLess is lexicographic byte ordering; buzz has no `<` on str, so the sibling pager spells it out to sort filenames deterministically.

nodes.label: strToNat
nodes.doc: strToNat parses a decimal digit string to a non-negative int, ignoring non-digits. Used for semver segment parsing.

nodes.label: stripTags
nodes.doc: stripTags removes HTML tags, leaving text. Entities goldmark produced stay encoded, so the result drops into a double-quoted attribute (TOC link tooltips) without re-escaping.

nodes.label: truncateWords
nodes.doc: truncateWords caps s at about n characters, cutting on a word boundary so it never ends mid-word. Short paragraphs pass through.

nodes.label: allDigits
nodes.doc: allDigits reports whether every byte of s is an ASCII digit (and s is non-empty).

nodes.label: blogDateDirectory
nodes.doc: blogDateDirectory turns a YYYY-MM-DD- prefix into nested "YYYY/MM/DD", or null.

nodes.label: blogSlug
nodes.doc: blogSlug drops a leading YYYY-MM-DD- date prefix, leaving the title slug.

nodes.label: blogURLPath
nodes.doc: blogURLPath is a post's URL path below blog/: date scope + slug, or just the slug.

nodes.label: cleanDepth
nodes.doc: cleanDepth is the segment count of a page's clean URL (how many "../" reach root).

nodes.label: cleanURL
nodes.doc: cleanURL maps a docs-relative source path to its clean gen-root URL: drop .md, drop a trailing index/README/_index landing, add a slash. Blog posts route through blogURLPath for date scoping. "" for the home page. The docs tree carries no "gen" segment (the walk skips the output dir by name; generated markdown lands in real content dirs), so source path maps straight to URL with no build-segment flattening.

nodes.label: hasDatePrefix
nodes.doc: hasDatePrefix detects a leading YYYY-MM-DD- prefix (11 chars) on a slugged filename.

nodes.label: tagSlug
nodes.doc: tagSlug turns an author-written tag into one URL segment: "remote cache" -> "remote-cache", "magus.yaml" -> "magus-yaml". Tags are prose, so two that differ only in punctuation or case are the same topic and must land on the same page - kebabCase is what collapses them.

nodes.label: build
nodes.doc: build renders the site: the tree cd.yaml publishes and deploy-generate assembles. None of it is committed, so unlike generate it is gated by producing without error rather than by a byte comparison - see generate's comment for the split.  generate first, because site-generate reads the Markdown and catalog it derives. The esbuild bundles are NOT listed here: site-generate declares them itself, which is what makes it correct when something other than this target invokes it. Repeating them would state the ord

nodes.label: build_hljs
nodes.doc: build-hljs bundles the vendored highlight.js library (src/vendor/hljs.js -> highlight.js@11) into gen/assets/hljs.js. syntax-highlight.js imports it same-origin so syntax highlighting works offline without any CDN. Bump the version in package.json and the next generate picks it up; gen/ is not committed, so generate runs this as one of its stages.

nodes.label: build_playground
nodes.doc: build-playground rebuilds the WebAssembly interpreter the playground loads: the stock Go toolchain compiles ../cmd/buzz-playground straight into gen/playground/buzz.wasm, and Go's own wasm_exec.js glue is copied beside it. The glue must come from the SAME Go that built the wasm - it is a matched pair.  gen/, not vendor/. Those bytes were committed for one reason: CI had no TinyGo, so it could not reproduce them and they had to be inputs rather than output. CI has Go. So this is ordinary render output now, r

nodes.label: build_playground_editor
nodes.doc: build-playground-editor bundles the CodeMirror editor the playground loads into gen/playground/editor.js. It existed only as a pnpm script before, because the artifact was committed and a human ran it after a version bump. gen/ is no longer committed, so every published byte needs a target CI can run - a script nothing invokes would have shipped a playground with no editor.

nodes.label: buzz_test
nodes.doc: buzz-test runs render's in-file `test "..." {}` blocks through `magus buzz`, in --embedded mode so render's markdown/encoding imports resolve. magus.cmd raises on a non-zero exit, so a failing assertion fails this target.

nodes.label: content_generate
nodes.doc: content-generate regenerates the committed docs Markdown derived from the Go source tree: the Buzz stdlib module reference (cmd/magus-docs, from the host module registry), the built-in spell reference plus the spells.md table (cmd/magus-spelldocs), the Markdown manpages (cmd/magus-manpage -format md, from internal/cli), and the worked examples in knowledge.md (cmd/magus-examples, captured from a fixture graph). The generator tools live at the repo root, so they run from here (the docs cwd) through the go sp

nodes.label: conventions
nodes.doc: conventions holds the prose corpus to the conventions page it publishes: no shell prompt in a command block, no pinned version standing in for example output, no backticked path that has since moved. See docs/conventions.md for what each rule means.  Its OWN target, not a line inside lint, and it deliberately depends on nothing. A prose nit should name the thing that is wrong; folding it into lint would report a stale path in the README as "docs lint failed", and a target that fails for reasons unrelated to

nodes.label: diagrams_generate
nodes.doc: diagrams-generate writes the committed light/dark SVG pair for every diagram under diagrams/. The docs site does NOT read these - it inlines a CSS-variable copy at render time so a diagram follows the theme toggle. This pair is for GitHub, where the README loads an image through and cannot reach the page's CSS at all. The pair lands under this project rather than beside the terminal recordings in the workspace's assets/gen: docs already depends on the root project, so writing there is MGS1012, a targ

nodes.label: format
nodes.doc: Scope dprint by ARGV, not by its config, for the same reason the root project does: dprint DISCOVERS a nested dprint.json and formats that subtree under its own config, and neither this project's `includes` nor an exclude prunes it. Since the guard-hook templates' project under guides/integrations/agents grew Markdown pages of its own, a bare run here reached them - the parent target writing into a descendant project, which magus rejects as MGS3001. That project formats its own pages.  Keep this list in ste

nodes.label: generate
nodes.doc: generate owns the COMMITTED derived files, and nothing else. That is the line between generate and build here: generate's output is in the repository, so CI can re-run it and fail when the bytes move, and the drift gate below is that check. build's output is not committed, so no comparison can gate it - it is verified by rendering without error.  The site render, the esbuild bundles, and the WebAssembly playground all write the ignored gen/ tree, so they live in build. They used to run here, which cost ever

nodes.label: index_generate
nodes.doc: index-generate refreshes MAGUS.md (the target catalog + dependency graph) from this magusfile, so it stays in lockstep with the targets. generate calls it; run standalone after editing targets: `magus run index-generate docs`.

nodes.label: install
nodes.doc: pnpm, NOT npm: .npmrc's minimum-release-age supply-chain gate is the reason. Always let pnpm validate the install. A canceled or interrupted install leaves a node_modules directory that EXISTS but is incomplete, so the `if (!fs.isDir(...))` guard this replaced read that tree as ready and handed the missing packages to esbuild instead - surfacing as `Could not resolve "@codemirror/view"` from build-playground-editor, which reads like a source bug rather than a half-installed tree. On a warm tree --frozen-loc

nodes.label: lint
nodes.doc: lint runs the client-side TypeScript gates: tsc for type errors and Biome for the banned patterns (no `any`, no non-null assertions - see biome.json). Both need node_modules, which it reaches through format -> generate -> preflight; proc.exec raises on a non-zero exit, so either gate fails lint.  Markdown formatting is dprint, run once from the root project (its scope is dprint.json at the workspace root), so `format` here is a dependency edge and nothing else. This project only lints prose; see docs/concep

nodes.label: render
nodes.doc: render is the fast docs/blog iteration path; it skips generated content, bundles, and drift checks.

nodes.label: security
nodes.doc: security audits what actually ships against the npm advisory database. See console/magusfile.buzz for why it is --prod, why it is not folded into lint, and why the .npmrc cooling period is the stronger half of this.

nodes.label: site_generate
nodes.doc: site-generate owns publication. It cannot replay while it reads VCS state; the public generate target still lets the independent content stages fan out first.  The bundles are needed HERE, not merely ordered by whoever calls this. They used to be ordered only in `generate`, which made this target correct as a stage and broken on its own: `magus run site-generate docs` - and `magus vcs resolve`, which invokes the target that owns a conflicted output directly - failed on `playground/index.html references miss

nodes.label: esbuild
nodes.doc: esbuild runs the pinned esbuild binary with an exact argv.  proc\exec, not os\execute(["sh", "-c", ...]): the shell form spawned a second process per call purely to parse a string this code had just finished building, and every path went through it as an interpolated command-line token rather than an argument. It also swallowed failures - os\execute RETURNS the exit code, and none of these calls read it, so a broken bundle wrote nothing and the render carried on to fail later somewhere else. proc\exec raise

nodes.label: generateJsBundles
nodes.doc: generateJsBundles builds the committed browser bundles that import npm packages. pnpm is pinned by package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, and --frozen-lockfile runs every time rather than behind an isDir check: an interrupted install leaves a node_modules that exists but is incomplete, and the guard read that as ready and fed esbuild a half tree. See the install() note in magusfile.buzz.

nodes.label: site_conventions
nodes.doc: site_publish is the cacheable publication unit used by docs:site-generate. Keep every output that belongs to the completed site in this one phase: the page tree, pnpm-backed vendor bundles, the integrity manifest, and (only for rw) the URL ledger. site_conventions re-exports the gates check for the magusfile. engine/gates is flat-imported here, and a flat import does not RE-export, so the magusfile cannot reach conventionsCheck through this module without a wrapper.

nodes.label: site_diagram_drift
nodes.doc: site_diagram_drift forwards the diagram-to-code check, for the same reason site_diagrams does: engine/page owns the single import of the registry.

nodes.label: site_diagrams
nodes.doc: site_diagrams writes the committed light/dark SVG pair for the magusfile's diagrams-generate target, forwarding to engine/page, which owns the registry import.

nodes.label: site_render
nodes.doc: site_render rebuilds gen/ from ../docs and the root README. Pure function of git history (footers) and the source tree - reproducible and gate-stable.

nodes.label: walk
nodes.doc: Recursively walk docs/ (the render reads its co-located markdown; the SSG's own root children - gen/, src/, tour/, node_modules/, MAGUS.md - are skipped at the root).

nodes.label: walkBlog
nodes.doc: walkBlog visits every publishable blog/*.md post (isPublishablePost: not the index, not an _underscored fixture, not `draft: true`) in fs.list's sorted order, so the walk is deterministic. Posts are flat: no nested subdirs under blog/.

nodes.label: magusConfig
nodes.doc: Nav links in display order; Console opens blank (new tab) - it is a standalone app, not a docs page.

nodes.label: collectDevelopmentPages
nodes.doc: collectDevelopmentPages registers EVERY /development/ page in docPages before anything renders, the same pre-walk contract collectDocPages and collectSectionIndexes hold.  Registering at render time (which is what renderDevelopmentPage used to do) cannot work here, because the section's two navigation directions point at each other: the landing's "In this section" list is built from its children, and every child's list is built from the landing that governs it. Whichever rendered second was the only one wit

nodes.label: projectCatalog
nodes.doc: projectCatalog renders one project's target catalog as Markdown from the TYPED graph (TargetGraphProject) rather than by capturing `describe graph -o markdown` from a subprocess. Building it here means the page is assembled from the same in-process data the CLI renders, with no fork, no stdout to re-parse, and compile-checked field access on every node.  An inline SVG figure draws the run order from each node's declared dependencies, so the arrows are the real ctx.needs edges and not a hand-maintained pictu

nodes.label: projectLabel
nodes.doc: projectLabel is the display name for a workspace-relative project path. The root project's path is ".", which reads as nothing at all in a URL, a card, or a graph node; every render site here goes through this so they cannot disagree.

nodes.label: projectPageDesc
nodes.doc: projectPageDesc is one project page's description. Same reason as the constants above: two passes, one string.

nodes.label: registerDevPage
nodes.doc: registerDevPage adds a synthesized /development/ page to docPages, the corpus every navigation helper walks. addRecord alone only feeds the search index, so without this these pages were reachable by search and invisible to Related, the section list, and the subtree.  The landing page is the section's overview, so it anchors the others rather than listing itself.

nodes.label: renderDevelopment
nodes.doc: renderDevelopment writes the /development/ section BELOW its landing: one themed page per project rendering its target catalog and run-order graph, the Contributing guide, and a /development/projects/ index linking to the project pages and showing how they depend on each other. Retired /development/projects/<slug> URLs redirect to the flattened locations.  The section LANDING is not written here - /development/ is the repository README, which renderRoot writes. That is why this file no longer carries a buil

nodes.label: renderDevelopmentPage
nodes.doc: renderDevelopmentPage renders one /development/ page from markdown through the shared renderPage() pipeline (nav, TOC, theme, search index). url ends in "/"; srcRel uses the "<dir>/_index.md" marker so rootPrefix/renderBreadcrumb derive the right depth and trail. collectDevelopmentPages has already registered it.

nodes.label: renderDevelopmentPageRaw
nodes.doc: renderDevelopmentPageRaw is renderDevelopmentPage for bodies already in final HTML (the /development/projects/ landing). It skips renderContentHTML - whose link-rewrite strips the trailing slash off relative links - so card hrefs like "../magus/" stay slash-terminated and resolve without a directory redirect. searchText is the plain text to index, since the HTML carries no useful prose.

nodes.label: slugifyProject
nodes.doc: slugifyProject turns a workspace-relative project path into one URL segment: "libs/gopherbuzz" -> "libs-gopherbuzz". Nested projects are the reason this exists -- the previous shallow scan never produced a path with a separator in it.  split/join, not replace: str.replace substitutes only the FIRST match, so a two-separator path ("cmd/magus/starter") kept the rest and the "one segment" this promises became a directory tree - /development/cmd-magus/starter/ - plus a node id with slashes still in it.

nodes.label: workspaceDependencies
nodes.doc: workspaceDependencies renders how the PROJECTS relate, as Markdown. The per-project pages answer "what can I run here"; this answers "what does changing it reach", which no page showed before.  It reads magus.projectGraph()'s typed view: nodes already in topological order (so the table IS a valid build order, sorted by nobody here), each node's direct dependencies, and its blast radius - the count of projects a change can transitively affect, which is the number that tells a contributor whether an edit is c

nodes.label: inlinePageDiagrams
nodes.doc: inlinePageDiagrams swaps any diagram reference on a page for the inline SVG. Guarded on the page mentioning one first: renderAll walks every figure in the registry, and a docs build renders hundreds of pages that reference none.

nodes.label: markedIds
nodes.doc: markedIds pulls each id following a marker. The id runs to the first space or end of line, so a marker may carry a trailing note explaining what the box is called.

nodes.label: renderAll
nodes.doc: renderAll returns the inline, theme-following SVG for each diagram, keyed by id, ready for inlineDiagrams. Throws on the first diagram that fails validation, which is what makes a crooked figure fail the docs build rather than ship.  The result is memoized and shared by every caller, so treat it as read-only.

nodes.label: verifyAnchors
nodes.doc: verifyAnchors checks both directions of the diagram-to-code link and returns one message per break, empty when they agree.  Forward: every anchor a diagram declares must still resolve to a path in the tree. This is the half that catches the common rot - a package renamed or deleted while the figure keeps naming it.  Reverse: every magus:diagram marker in the sources must name a diagram that exists. This is the half that catches a diagram being renamed or dropped while call sites still point at it. Neither h

nodes.label: writeStandalonePair
nodes.doc: writeStandalonePair writes the committed light/dark SVG files for every diagram into dir. These exist for GitHub: a README image is loaded through , which makes it a separate document with no access to the page's CSS variables, so the palette has to be baked in and a second file is the only way to offer a dark one. Naming follows the terminal recordings already in assets/gen: the unsuffixed file is dark and carries the fallback, `-light` is the prefers-color-scheme: light source.

nodes.label: renderDownloadPage
nodes.doc: renderDownloadPage writes gen/download/index.html.  Every link is relative and resolves one level up, since the page sits at download/ rather than at gen's root: the asset gate proves each target exists, so a renamed setup guide fails the build here rather than 404ing for a reader mid-install.

nodes.label: recentPosts
nodes.doc: recentPosts renders up to three of the newest blog posts as cards, or "" when the blog is empty.  It reads the posts' frontmatter directly rather than using site.blogPosts, and the reason is ordering: walkBlog fills that list well after renderLanding runs, so at this point it is empty. Reading here keeps the landing independent of where the blog sits in the render sequence, which is worth more than the few lines saved by sharing - a "recent posts" block that silently renders nothing because a step moved is

nodes.label: renderLanding
nodes.doc: renderLanding writes gen/index.html. srcRel is LANDING_SRC, the synthetic source path every "is this the home page" test in renderPage keys off; it maps to the empty clean URL, so the chrome resolves at gen's root and no breadcrumb is drawn.  Every link here is relative and points at a page this render also writes - the asset gate proves that, and the orphan gate walks outward from exactly this page, so the four sections below are what make the rest of the site reachable at all.

nodes.label: loadReleases
nodes.doc: loadReleases builds site.releases, newest-first.  TAGS ARE THE SPINE. A release exists because someone tagged it, so the version list and its dates come from vcs\tags("v*"); the glob keeps release tags and skips namespaced ones (backup/x, pre-rebase-main), whose wildcards stop at "/".  releases/v*.yaml is ENRICHMENT layered on top, carrying the two things a tag cannot know: the changelog prose the Atom feed renders, and the artifact name/platform/size/sha256 that gen/public/release/index.json publishes for

nodes.label: renderPublic
nodes.doc: renderPublic writes /public/ - one ordinary page listing the machine-readable endpoints this site serves. It used to be four nested Apache-mod_autoindex listings (public/, public/atom/, public/release/, public/release/<ver>/) whose columns promised more than the site delivers: the per-version pages tabulated artifact names, sizes, and checksums for files that are hosted on GitHub and were never served from here, so each one rendered a directory listing of an empty directory. Releases now link to the GitHub

nodes.label: artifactDesc
nodes.doc: artifactDesc describes a release artifact from its filename and platform, over the standard release asset set.

nodes.label: isVersionTag
nodes.doc: isVersionTag reports whether a git tag names a release: "v" followed by three dot-separated numeric parts, with an optional -prerelease/+build suffix on the last one ("v0.3.0", "v1.0.0-rc.1"). Anything else is some other kind of tag.  This exists because a `v*` refspec is NOT a version filter, and reading it as one shipped a real bug: a tag called "verified-refinements" matched the glob, sorted newest by creation date, and became site.releases[0]. That is the value the announcement bar prints AND the value

nodes.label: semverSortKey
nodes.doc: semverSortKey returns a zero-padded sort key: "v0.10.0.yaml" -> "0000.0010.0000", so lexicographic order matches numeric semver. Unknown formats fall through to the original name (safe: sort-only).

nodes.label: sortNamesSemverDesc
nodes.doc: sortNamesSemverDesc sorts release filenames newest-first. Selection sort; O(n^2) fine for ~10-20 releases. Mirrors Go's compareSemver in cmd/magus-utils/release.go.

nodes.label: collectSectionIndexes
nodes.doc: collectSectionIndexes appends a DocPage for every directory that has pages beneath it but no page of its own. Registering before the walk is what makes the synthesized page a first-class citizen: breadcrumbs resolve through it, the section nav lists its children, Related can rank against it, and the subtree finally has something to hang off.  An authored overview always wins - if concepts.md exists, nothing is synthesized for concepts/.

nodes.label: parentPrefixes
nodes.doc: parentPrefixes returns every ancestor directory URL of a page URL, each with a trailing slash: "a/b/c/" -> ["a/", "a/b/"]. The page's own URL is excluded; a page is not its own parent.

nodes.label: renderSectionIndexes
nodes.doc: renderSectionIndexes writes each synthesized overview: a card per direct child, title and description, same shape as the Related grid so the two read as one vocabulary rather than two.  Only DIRECT children get cards. The full branch is already in the sidebar's "Everything here" list, which this page now qualifies for, so repeating the whole subtree in the body would say the same thing twice at different sizes.

nodes.label: sectionTitle
nodes.doc: sectionTitle turns a URL segment into a heading: "targets" -> "Targets", "ci-providers" -> "Ci providers". Deliberately dumb - a section that wants a better name should get a real authored page, which this then steps aside for.
